To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the full sequence or core of nestin gene promoter with intron- 2 is a potential candidate for the specific regulation of exogenous genes expression in NSCs.

the full sequence or core of the nestin promoter can regulate the expression of EGPF in nestin-positive and negative cells and can only regulate the expression of the EGFP in nestin-positive cell when the full sequence of nestin promoter is fused with introns.

the full sequence (including the 5' flanking region and 3' flanking region of the nestin promoter) of the nestin-specific gene promoter which is linked to the intron-2 sequence can specifically regulate the EGFP in nestin-positive cell lines, but not nestin-negative cell lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the regulatory mechanism of the nestin-specific promoter.
the identification of nestin gene promoter elements and provides a theoretical basis for the construction of nestin gene regulatory vectors and for the development of gene therapy for brain tumors.
the construction of a specific regulatory element of the nestin promoter and the study of its function in regulating the expression of exogenic genes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nestin gene full sequence which was fused with its intron-2 is an excellent candidate for a NSC-specific regulatory promoter element.
intron-2 is an important regulatory element for the nestin gene and that it is a key factor in determining the nestin gene expression specificity.
intron-2 is an essential element in the regulation of gene expression in nestin positive cells, which is consistent with the results of previous studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the full sequence (or the core sequence) of the nestin promoter which is fused to intron-2 may be a good candidate for the construction of a nestin gene-specific regulatory promoter element.

the full sequence or core sequences of the nestin promoter can be used to regulate gene expression in NSCs and the full sequence of nestin promoter which is fused intron-2 may be used to specifically regulate the expression in NSCs.
the full sequence (4000 bp) of the nestin promoter is not enough for specific regulation of exogenous genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the full sequence or core sequences of the nestin promoter can be used to regulate the exogenous gene expression in nestin-negative cells.
we can use nestin gene promoter to specifically regulate the expression level of exogenous genes.
the core sequence of nestin gene promoter can also be used to specifically regulate exogenous gene expression in nestin positive cells.
